ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Grass sliding is a recreational activity. In a certain grass sliding field, the middle is a flat lawn, and there are slopes on both the left and right sides. The process of tourists sliding on this field is modeled as shown in Figure B (the tourist and the sliding board are treated as a single point mass). A tourist slides down from point D on the left slope, reaches the bottom point C, passes through a $10\mathrm{m}$ long flat lawn, and arrives at the bottom point B of the right slope with a speed of $10\mathrm{m/s}$. It is known that the angle between the right slope and the horizontal plane is $37^{\circ}$, and the coefficient of kinetic friction between the sliding board and all the grass surfaces is 0.5. (Given $\sin37^{\circ}=0.6$, $\cos37^{\circ}=0.8$), find:

1. What is the speed $v$ of the tourist sliding down the left slope to point C at the bottom?
2. What is the time $t$ that the tourist slides on the right slope?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the left side is a section of slope, point D is above the left slope, and point C is at the bottom end of the left slope; in the middle, from C to B is horizontal grassland; on the right side, from B upward to A is the right slope, and the angle between the right slope and the horizontal dashed line is labeled θ. At C, a velocity v to the right is drawn, indicating that after the tourist slides from the left slope to C, the tourist moves rightward along the horizontal section and enters the right slope at B. Reasoning calculation: Take the data given by the problem and method: BC=10 m, the speed of the tourist when reaching B is v_B=10 m/s, the coefficient of kinetic friction μ=0.5, the right-slope angle θ=37°, sin37°=0.6, cos37°=0.8, and take g=10 m/s² according to the method. 1. On the horizontal section from C to B, only kinetic friction acts to decelerate, the magnitude of the horizontal acceleration is μg=0.5×10=5 m/s², and its direction is opposite to the direction of motion, so a=-5 m/s². From the uniformly varied motion relation v_B²-v_C²=2as, obtain: 10²-v_C²=2×(-5)×10=-100, therefore v_C²=200, v_C=10√2 m/s. 2. On the right slope, the tourist first slides upward from B at 10 m/s. The component of gravity down along the slope is mg sinθ, and friction also acts down along the slope, so the deceleration is a_up=g(sinθ+μcosθ)=10×(0.6+0.5×0.8)=10 m/s². The time required to slide upward to stop is t_up=v_B/a_up=10/10=1 s, and the upward sliding distance is s=v_B²/(2a_up)=100/(20)=5 m. Then the tourist slides down along the right slope from the highest point, with initial speed 0. At this time, the acceleration down along the slope is a_down=g(sinθ-μcosθ)=10×(0.6-0.5×0.8)=10×0.2=2 m/s². Sliding down the same distance 5 m gives 5=(1/2)×2×t_down², so t_down=√5 s. The total time on the right slope is t=t_up+t_down=1+√5 s.
